subject: chemistry
question_text: Classify the oxide Tl₂O₃ as neutral, acidic, basic or amphoteric.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students — Chemistry (2026-27 edition), book p.104, chapter 9 p-BLOCK ELEMENTS GROUP 14, Very Short Answer Questions question 4(g). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints no per-step allocation on any answer in this chapter. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book's classification of Tl₂O₃ as basic is correct and is what this card gives. The group-13 run written on this card — B₂O₃ acidic, Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ amphoteric, In₂O₃ and Tl₂O₃ basic — is NCERT's, and is carried here because the class of a single oxide is easiest to hold as part of the trend. The acid equation was atom-counted: Tl₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2TlCl₃ + 3H₂O has Tl 2, O 3, H 6, Cl 6 on each side. This book prints no exam-appearance years for this chapter, so appearances[] is empty.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The classification
lines: Thallium(III) oxide Tl₂O₃ is a basic
A basic oxide reacts with an acid to give
It gives no salt with an alkali.
steps.why: Thallium is the heaviest and most metallic member of group 13, and a metallic element gives a basic oxide. A reaction with an acid, together with no reaction with a base, is exactly what separates a basic oxide from an amphoteric one.
common_mistakes: Calling Tl₂O₃ amphoteric because Al₂O₃ is. Tl₂O₃ reacts with an acid but not with an alkali, so it is basic.

Writing TlCl as the salt in this equation. Tl₂O₃ has thallium at +3, so the chloride formed here is TlCl₃; the +1 chloride TlCl is the one the inert pair effect makes more stable, but it is not the product of this reaction.
steps.memory_tip: The heaviest member is the most metallic, and a metallic element gives a basic oxide.
steps.margin_note: The acid equation with no alkali reaction is what makes the oxide basic.

steps.label: The trend down group 13
lines: Down group 13 the oxides change class as
B₂O₃ is acidic, Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ are
amphoteric, In₂O₃ and Tl₂O₃ are basic.

lines.text: Basic character: B < Al < Ga < In < Tl

steps.why: The class of an oxide follows the metallic character of the element, and metallic character rises down a group as the atoms get larger and the ionisation enthalpy falls. Writing the whole run from boron to thallium shows the answer as a trend rather than one fact remembered for one oxide.
common_mistakes: Writing that every group 13 oxide is amphoteric because Al₂O₃ is. Only aluminium and gallium give amphoteric oxides.
Reversing the trend and calling B₂O₃ basic. Boron is the least metallic member and its oxide is the acidic one.
steps.memory_tip: Acidic at the top, basic at the bottom: B₂O₃ acidic, Tl₂O₃ basic.
steps.margin_note: One line of trend from boron to thallium places the oxide inside the group.

insider_note: Down group 13 the oxides go from acidic to basic as the metallic character rises: B₂O₃ acidic, Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ amphoteric, In₂O₃ and Tl₂O₃ basic. Thallium is at the far end of that run, so the class is easiest to hold as part of the trend rather than as one fact on its own.
